what: Netskope secures internet traffic for companies. Instead of routing staff through a corporate network, its service inspects every connection in the cloud, blocking threats and stopping confidential data leaving.
customers: Large enterprises with staff working from anywhere, on subscriptions priced per user.
money: the cloud security platform, priced per user per year
moat: Traffic inspection points placed inside a customer's network path, plus data classification policies tuned over time. Replacing it means re-routing every employee's internet connection.
risks: A $737M net loss on $803M of revenue, much of it stock compensation after the 2025 listing
13 times sales, and the analyst average target is below the current price
Palo Alto and Cisco bundle similar capability into platforms customers already buy
opportunities: Revenue grew from $407M to $709M in two years
Free cash flow is close to breakeven at minus $70M, so the loss is mostly non-cash
watch: Annual recurring revenue growth and the path to positive free cash flow.
